suite: SEC lane wave — security reference corpora
pre_registered: 2026-10-03 (before retrieval; committed to corpus-hub prior to the retrieval run)
authoring: BLIND from clone reads; every expect is a verbatim clause (<=25 words) grep-verified against the clone at authoring time; no retrieval was run

ghsa-db.shape_risk: Content shape is ideal — one JSON per GHSA id under advisories/ with the largest at 143 KB — but the corpus is 380k tiny files plus a 216 MB .git pack, and unreviewed/ mirrors github-reviewed/ records, so duplicate hits on the same CVE are plausible.

queries.q: In the npm advisory GHSA-jf85-cpcp-j695 for lodash, what does exploiting the flaw do to properties on every object?
queries.expect: causing the addition or modification of an existing property that will exist on all objects

queries.q: Under what conditions does rust-openssl before 0.10.79 overrun an allocation, and by how much?
queries.expect: writes up to 7 bytes past the end of the caller's buffer or Vec

queries.q: When does the python requests library expose proxy credentials to a target server, per GHSA-j8r2-6x86-q33q?
queries.expect: vulnerable to potentially leaking `Proxy-Authorization` headers to destination servers, specifically during redirects to an HTTPS origin

queries.q: What is the worst-case outcome of loading a hostile .pth checkpoint into PyTorch, per GHSA-63cw-57p8-fm3p?
queries.expect: can corrupt memory and potentially lead to arbitrary code execution

queries.q: What can an external user of esm.sh's CDN do to intranet-only sites via GHSA-3c9r-837r-qqm4?
queries.expect: allowing an attacker to retrieve information from internal websites through the vulnerability

ghsa-db.note: expect_files re-based 2026-10-04 to the scoped-mirror layout (xerj-org/corpus-ghsa-db drops the upstream 'advisories/' segment; queries and expect clauses unchanged)

pysec.shape_risk: Max file 36 KB, one YAML per advisory under vulns/<package>/ — clean per-file shape, but details blocks are YAML-folded across lines (verbatim clauses need whitespace-normalized matching) and 2026-era advisories embed long markdown writeups that may swamp chunks.

queries.q: What root cause did the django advisory for CVE-2024-56374 give for the denial of service?
queries.expect: Lack of upper-bound limit enforcement in strings passed when performing IPv6 validation

queries.q: Why did urllib3 2.0.5 ship a fix for CVE-2023-43804, and what did it prevent?
queries.expect: unknowingly leak information via HTTP redirects to a different origin if that user doesn't disable redirects explicitly

queries.q: What happens to my python process if it deserializes a hostile PKCS7 blob with the affected cryptography release?
queries.expect: Calling `load_pem_pkcs7_certificates` or `load_der_pkcs7_certificates` could lead to a NULL-pointer dereference and segfault

queries.q: What did CVE-2026-25645 let a local attacker pre-plant in the temp folder used by requests?
queries.expect: uses a predictable filename when extracting files from zip archives into the system temporary directory

queries.q: What kind of malicious upload header triggered the regular expression denial of service fixed in FastAPI?
queries.expect: An attacker could send a custom-made `Content-Type` option that is very difficult for the RegEx to process

go-vulndb.shape_risk: 4.6k per-ID OSV JSONs under data/osv/ (largest 13 KB) are well-shaped, but the clone also ships the entire vulndb Go tool source, tests and testdata (largest file 15 MB .gz), so non-advisory files can soak up retrieval hits.

queries.q: What could a malicious client forge through gin's URL handling per GO-2020-0001?
queries.expect: allows attackers to inject arbitrary log entries by manipulating the request path

queries.q: Why did Go 1.19.6 patch the x/net HTTP/2 code — what resource does GO-2023-1571 burn?
queries.expect: cause excessive CPU consumption in the HPACK decoder, sufficient to cause a denial of service from a small number of small requests

queries.q: What hang did google.golang.org/protobuf fix in 1.33.0 per GO-2024-2611?
queries.expect: can enter an infinite loop when unmarshaling certain forms of invalid JSON

queries.q: What input makes Go's TLS stack crash before the 1.16.6 fix?
queries.expect: clients can panic when provided a certificate of the wrong type for the negotiated parameters

queries.q: What kind of message remotely crashes an unauthenticated Go SSH endpoint when AEAD ciphers are in use?
queries.expect: consuming a malformed packet which contains an empty plaintext causes a panic

mitre-attck.shape_risk: Monolith-shaped: every matrix ships as one giant STIX bundle (enterprise-attack.json is 53.8 MB, and 42 near-duplicate versioned enterprise bundles exist) with NO per-object files, so retrieval may simply fail on shape — expects are anchored to the smallest bundles (mobile 1.0/3.0 at 0.7-1.2 MB, ics 8.0/9.0 at 1.3-1.5 MB) plus one deliberate 53.8 MB enterprise probe.

queries.q: What does the ATT&CK ICS technique Project File Infection achieve on a controller once code is planted?
queries.expect: Malicious programs allow adversaries control of all aspects of the process enabled by the PLC

queries.q: During an OT intrusion, how can an adversary blind control-room staff while the underlying operations keep running?
queries.expect: The environment's data and processes may still be operational, but functioning in an unintended or adversarial manner

queries.q: What does the Pegasus implant do on an iPhone according to its ATT&CK mobile entry?
queries.expect: escalates privileges on iOS devices and uses its privileged access to collect a variety of sensitive information

queries.q: What can a hostile Android application achieve by exploiting the operating system's accessibility framework, per ATT&CK mobile?
queries.expect: A malicious app could abuse Android's accessibility features to capture sensitive data or perform other malicious actions

queries.q: According to Enterprise ATT&CK, how does the Phishing technique ultimately run attacker payloads?
queries.expect: Adversaries may send victims emails containing malicious attachments or links, typically to execute malicious code on victim systems

owasp-cheatsheets.shape_risk: 136 markdown files, largest 74 KB — friendly shape; the real risk is topical overlap between sibling sheets (XSS vs DOM-based XSS vs XSS Filter Evasion, five Authorization sheets), which makes near-duplicate chunks plausible.

queries.q: What Argon2id work parameters does the OWASP cheat sheet recommend for storing passwords?
queries.expect: with a minimum configuration of 19 MiB of memory, an iteration count of 2, and 1 degree of parallelism

queries.q: Why does OWASP push parameterized queries as the main defense for database injection flaws?
queries.expect: prepared statements ensure that an attacker cannot change the intent of a query, even if SQL commands are inserted by an attacker

queries.q: After login, how much is a session cookie worth compared to the credentials the user just presented?
queries.expect: is temporarily equivalent to the strongest authentication method used by the application

queries.q: Is there a CSRF mitigation for my fetch-based frontend that avoids anti-forgery tokens entirely?
queries.expect: A user-friendly defense that is particularly well suited for AJAX or API endpoints is the use of a **custom request header**

queries.q: Why is trusting the alg field dangerous when a REST endpoint validates a JSON web token?
queries.expect: It must not rely on the information of the JWT header to select the verification algorithm

owasp-asvs.shape_risk: 29 chapter markdowns in 5.0/en (largest 23 KB), but the repo also carries 4.0-era chapters, five language translations, and docs_en flat JSON/CSV/XML renderings of the identical requirement text — heavy duplicate risk across versions and formats.

queries.q: What does ASVS level 2 say about protecting the SMS or email verification channel from automated guessing?
queries.expect: a code based out-of-band authentication mechanism is protected against brute force attacks by using rate limiting

queries.q: How much randomness must a server-side session reference have under ASVS?
queries.expect: generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) and possess at least 128 bits of entropy

queries.q: What does ASVS require apps to do about restricting which JWT signing methods they accept?
queries.expect: The allowlist must include the permitted algorithms, ideally only either symmetric or asymmetric algorithms, and must not include the 'None' algorithm

queries.q: What extra transport-security requirement does ASVS impose at its highest assurance level?
queries.expect: L3 applications must only support cipher suites which provide forward secrecy

queries.q: How should an OAuth authorization server check callback URLs per ASVS?
queries.expect: validates redirect URIs based on a client-specific allowlist of pre-registered URIs using exact string comparison

owasp-wstg.shape_risk: 165 section markdowns under document/ (largest 45 KB) plus checklists, website and template copies of the same text — moderate duplicate risk; binary noise (ebooks/fonts, images) is confined to non-md paths.

queries.q: During database injection testing, what does the UNION technique accomplish?
queries.expect: to join a query, purposely forged by the tester, to the original query

queries.q: When testing tokens, what should happen if a payload section has been altered?
queries.expect: Modifying any part of the JWT should cause the signature to be invalid, and the token to be rejected by the server

queries.q: When testing login throttling, after how many failed tries do applications commonly freeze an account?
queries.expect: Accounts are typically locked after 3 to 5 unsuccessful attempts and can only be unlocked after a predetermined period of time

queries.q: What risks come from misconfigured permissions on cloud object stores like S3, per the testing guide?
queries.expect: may lead to the exposure of sensitive information, data tampering, or unauthorized access

queries.q: How can a tester map out every operation and type a GraphQL endpoint exposes?
queries.expect: Introspection queries are the method by which GraphQL lets you ask what queries are supported, which data types are available
